title: AIDA implementation build record
description: What `build-record` verified for one attempt at one unit, at <task folder>/implementation/build-<unit_id>.json (docs/implementation.md, 'The deciding checks run before anything judges'). One file per unit, holding only the latest attempt: a later attempt overwrites it, and `build-record` refuses to write it again for an attempt already recorded at the same commit (exit 45). This record runs all eight deciding checks: every test of this order passes, no test outside the baseline fails, the coding-standards tool is clean, static analysis is clean, the security tool is clean, the realized diff touches only files this order owns, every frozen test file is unchanged, and the interface record names every element the order's own declared interface names in backticks. A review only ever sees code that passed all eight, which is why none of them waits for a later step. The model writes the code; this file is the script's own half, verifying what came back rather than judging whether a criterion is met. Plain JSON, no fences, no markdown. A field present in a real record but absent from this schema's `properties` is a defect in the schema, not a value to silently accept, which is why `additionalProperties` is false.

schemaVersion.description: The shape this file was written in, the same field every other AIDA record carries.

takenAt.description: The UTC date this attempt was recorded, YYYY-MM-DD. Set by the script at the moment of writing, never typed by hand.

unit.description: The work order id this record belongs to, the same id `build-brief` was given and the file's own basename encodes (build-<unit_id>.json). Joined on, never re-minted.

startedAt.description: The commit this attempt began from, the full form of the `--started-at` value `build-record` was given, resolved and confirmed to name a real commit in the code repository (exit 43 otherwise). Check three's own diff runs from here to `commit`.

commit.description: The code repository's HEAD at the moment `build-record` ran, read fresh with `git rev-parse HEAD`, never assumed. Together with `attempt`, this is what exit 45 compares a new call against to refuse recording the same attempt twice.

attempt.description: Which attempt at this unit this is, one more than the ledger's own attemptsUsed before this call. `build-record` increments attemptsUsed after writing this record, whether the checks below were met or not: an attempt is a dispatch that ended, not a dispatch that succeeded.

interfaceRecord.description: The text at the path `--interface` named, copied verbatim. Check eight compares the countable half of it against the unit's own declared interface: every backtick-quoted token in the declaration must appear verbatim here. The rest of both texts is prose a person wrote, and the reviewer reads that. Required to be present and non-empty only when the unit's own frozen interface is non-empty (exit 44); otherwise this may be empty, including when no file was there to read.

reportPath.description: Where the builder's own report lives, copied from `--report` as given. Only the path is kept here, never the report's content: docs/implementation.md refuses the builder's account of what it did as authority, so this record never carries it as though it were evidence.

checks.description: The eight deciding checks this step runs, in a fixed order: order-tests, suite-regression, coding-standards, static-analysis, security, owned-files, frozen-tests, interface-record. Each carries its own verdict, so nothing downstream has to re-derive one from an exit code this file does not store on its own.

executed.description: How many of the checks in `checks` actually executed: they ran a command, which is every check carrying an exitCode, or they computed a diff or a hash, which is owned-files and frozen-tests. A frozen-tests row reading undeclared hashed no file, so it is not counted either: counting it would do the thing this field exists to stop. interface-record compares two texts the caller handed over and runs nothing, so it is never counted. The field exists because a record saying every check answered, without saying how many of them ran, reads the same whether the code was tested or nothing was.

recheckedAt.description: Present only after `build-recheck` ran the eight checks again over this record's own range, with no implementer dispatched and no attempt spent (live-run row 87): the UTC date of that run, YYYY-MM-DD. `checks`, `executed` and `decidingChecks` then hold the re-check's answers; `attempt`, `startedAt`, `commit` and `takenAt` stay the attempt's own.

checksBefore.description: Present with `recheckedAt`: the checks the re-check replaced, id and verdict only, so a reader can see what the re-check answered differently. The replaced outputs are not kept; the tool that refused a path printed nothing worth reading back.

decidingChecks.description: States plainly which of the deciding checks docs/implementation.md names this step ran. All eight of them, since 2026-09-11; the field stays because a reader must never have to count `checks` to learn what a pass here covered.

total.description: The number of deciding checks docs/implementation.md names in total. Always 8; a constant rather than a count of `checks`, so a step that ever ran fewer than all of them could not hide it.

ranHere.description: The `id` of each check in `checks`, in the same order, copied rather than re-derived, so a reader who only wants coverage never has to open `checks` to get it.

id.description: Which of the eight checks this is. The ids are in the same order docs/implementation.md names the checks in: order-tests and suite-regression are 'Every test of this order passes' and 'No test outside the baseline fails'; configuration-gate takes the order-tests slot on an order whose proof is gate: the `## Configuration gate` lines of the implement recipe, run in the worktree, met when every line exits 0, unmet naming the first line that did not, unknown when the task records no environment, no implement recipe was passed, or the recipe carries no such block (live-run row 65). It is the floor for such an order the way order-tests is for every other; done-when takes the same slot on an order whose proof is record: the judgement the checkpoint left on the order's ledger entry from its `--row <unit_id>=...`, met when confirmed, carrying `judgedBy` (person or model) so close can copy the judge, and on such an order suite-regression and the three tool checks read undeclared with a detail naming the proof, because a document in the task folder is nothing a suite or a tool reads (nyc defect 17); observed takes the same slot on an order whose proof is observe: the record the orchestrator wrote after a model looked at each of the order's surfaces at each viewport through a browser, passed as `--observed`, met when every row is met, unmet naming the first row that is not, unknown when the record cannot be read, carrying `judgedBy: model` so close copies the judge, and on such an order the suite and the tool rows run as they do for a code order (live-run row 104); coding-standards, static-analysis and security are the three tool checks; owned-files and frozen-tests are 'The realized diff touches only files this order owns' and 'Every frozen test file is unchanged'; interface-record is 'The interface record matches what the order declared'.

verdict.description: The four words every verdict in this stage uses, and one more that only suite-regression carries. deferred means the recipe costs its suite row end-of-task, so this attempt did not run it; finish runs the row once at the final commit and records the answer under finished.json's suite key (nyc defect 18). deferred passes the way undeclared does, because order-tests already ran this order's own frozen tests. undeclared means no resolved recipe carried a command for this check, or the recipe declared that row absent, or a tool row's own extensions list matched no file this order owns, or this order froze no test file so frozen-tests had nothing to hash, so the row did not apply here; undeclared is never satisfied and never a pass. order-tests carries a floor the others do not: it must have run and answered met, so undeclared or unknown there stops the attempt whatever the rest said, because an order nothing executed never reaches checks-passed. unknown means the check ran but nothing here can decide from it: its output held the --nothing-ran marker, so a selected-nothing exit 0 proved nothing; or the suite or a tool failed while the baseline already recorded that same framework or tool unknown or undeclared, or unmet with no output kept to subtract, so nothing here can tell that old finding from a new one this order introduced; or the command holds {paths} while this order declares no ownedFiles; or, for interface-record, the declaration names no element in backticks. Neither reads as met. unknown on interface-record is the one unknown that does not spend the attempt: it is a question for the reviewer, not a fault in the code. Every other unmet or unknown does.

absent.description: True when the recipe row for this tool was declared absent, and the reason in `detail` is the recipe's own. Absent from the entry otherwise. It exists because undeclared covers two facts that must not read alike: a framework that says it has no such tool answered the question, and a caller who passed no flag answered nothing. Both stay undeclared, because undeclared is never satisfied either way, and this field is what tells a reader which happened.

detail.description: Why this verdict, in plain words naming what was compared: an exit code, a set of file paths that did not match, or which marker or file could not be read.

framework.description: The framework whose resolved check recipe carried this tool row, present only on a tool check that had a command to run. One tool row may carry a command from one framework only: two frameworks each declaring one is refused before any check runs, because nothing here may choose between two answers to one question.
The framework this run belongs to, as project.json records it.

verdict.description: What this framework alone answered, before the verdicts were folded into the one above. deferred ranks above met in that fold: a suite one framework left to finish has not answered yet.

failureLine.description: Present only on suite-regression, and only when this framework's test-execution recipe declared failure_line on its suite row: the regular expression, as read from the recipe with its quotes stripped. The suite subtraction compared only the lines matching it, on both sides, so a reader can see which lines the verdict rests on.

runs.description: One entry per framework, present only on order-tests and suite-regression, which run once per framework the task resolved a test recipe for, because the build runs in one repository that is all of them at once. The check's own verdict is the worst of these, with undeclared ranking lowest so a framework that declared nothing never drags down one that ran and passed.

exitCode.description: What the check's own command exited with, present only for order-tests, suite-regression, coding-standards, static-analysis and security, and only when a command was actually supplied and run. Absent for owned-files, frozen-tests and interface-record, which compare files or text rather than run a command, and absent for a check left undeclared.

signal.description: Present only on a tool check whose recipe row declares it (dev-guides, process-recipes, '## Check commands' is parsed). empty-stdout marks a tool that cannot fail by exit status, gofmt -l being the case it was written for: a zero exit with anything on standard output counts as a failure, and a caller that ignores the key has a green light wired to nothing. That failure then goes through the same baseline comparison a non-zero exit does, because a finding the tool already reported at the commit the build started from is not one this order introduced.

extensions.description: Present only on a tool check whose recipe row declares it. The file extensions this tool reads; {paths} expanded to only the order's own owned files ending in one of them, because a tool handed a file type it does not read either skips it in silence or parses it as its own language and fails on it. An expansion that came out empty makes the verdict undeclared, never met: the row did not apply to this order.

paths.description: Present only on a tool check whose command held {paths} or {file}: the paths that token expanded to, relative to codePath, whether or not the command then ran. This order's owned files, a directory entry expanded to the files the repository tracks under it, minus its own frozen test files, minus any file the row's extensions exclude. The frozen tests come out because the implementer may not write them, a hook refuses it, so a finding in one is not this order's to fix; a reader compares this against the order's ownedFiles to see exactly what the tool judged.

frozenTestsLeftOut.description: Present only on a tool check whose command held {paths} or {file}, and only when at least one of this order's owned files is one of its own frozen tests: those paths, relative to codePath, which the tool was not handed. They are judged once, by the tests step before the freeze, and never here.

output.description: What the command printed, standard output and standard error together, verbatim, present under the same condition as exitCode. Kept whole and unmodified so a person or a later step can see exactly what the --nothing-ran marker check itself saw. A tool row carrying the signal empty-stdout has the two streams read apart and then joined, standard output first, so their interleaving is not preserved for that row.

newLines.description: Present only on suite-regression, coding-standards, static-analysis and security, and only when the baseline recorded that framework or tool unmet and the run now printed lines the baseline's own output did not hold: the first 20 of them, in the command's own words. Two lines are compared with every run of digits removed, runs of dots and whitespace squeezed and the ends trimmed, so a shifted line number, a count or a duration does not read as new. That is enough for a tool, whose output is one line per finding. It is not enough for a suite whose harness prints a progress line or a summary line that changes whenever a test is added or fixed, PHPUnit and pytest among them: on the whole output those read as new. A suite row that declares failure_line narrows the comparison to the lines that name a failed test, and runs[].failureLine records the selector used. These lines are what made the verdict unmet; a person reads them to see what this order introduced.

newLineCount.description: How many lines were new in all, present with newLines. newLines is capped at 20 and this is not.

judgedBy.description: Present only on done-when and observed. On done-when, who judged the order's done-when row at the checkpoint, copied from the ledger's own doneWhenJudgement so `close` writes the same judge on the criteria the order owns (nyc defect 17). On observed, always model: a model looked at the page, and the record says so (live-run row 104).
